impact_assessment.why: the pre-commit triad runs on the working tree, so a commit can contain less than what was tested: ADR-145 was committed without its implementation and a stale codebase map was committed twice today
impact_assessment.benefits: a broken commit is caught while it is still local, where PRINCIPLE-018 R5 undoes it with reset --soft instead of a revert, and the pushed history stays green for bisect and for anyone who checks out that commit
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new script and a new P018 rule; dependency: git worktree (already used by the kit's own tooling); concurrency: the worktree lives in the system temp dir, never inside the repository; state: none, the worktree is removed in a finally block
impact_assessment.mitigation: runner injected so unit tests spawn nothing; worktree removed even when a gate fails; one real end-to-end run recorded as evidence; integration test kept to the --help contract so the tier ceiling holds

[1/1] Switch AIKit from MIT to AGPL-3.0: replace LICENSE with the canonical AGPL text, update the README license line, record ADR-151, run the full delivery gates, commit and push non-destructively

impact_assessment.why: The project portfolio now uses AGPL-3.0, but AIKit itself, NeuralBeat and VoidFarer still expose MIT, Apache-2.0 and no license respectively, so the public repositories are inconsistent and GitHub cannot advertise the intended license
impact_assessment.benefits: One license across the portfolio, correct GitHub license detection, an explicit legal contract in every repository, and README/ADR records that match the shipped LICENSE
impact_assessment.risks: contract: AIKit moves from permissive MIT to copyleft AGPL-3.0; dependency: none; concurrency: another session may touch the shared root; state: no runtime state changes
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the canonical AGPL-3.0 text already staged in agpl_text.txt, keep the change to LICENSE/README/ADR, run the full AIKit gate set, stage explicitly, and push only after the commit is verified; abort on unrelated working-tree drift
